page: Amazon Web Services m6in.large is a general-purpose virtual server built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor. Allocated with 1 physical core and 2 vCPUs via multithreading, the instance provides 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It lacks integrated local NVMe storage and does not include discrete GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage architectures and baseline network throughput of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate moderate single-core efficiency paired with predictable entry-level throughput limitations. The instance achieves average performance tiers in single-threaded tests, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1651.0 and a stress-ng single-core rating of 1881.18. Hardware instruction support covers AVX-512 with VNNI, AES, and SHA extensions, assisting specialized cryptographic operations. However, aggregate multi-threaded metrics rank within the lower quartile, reflecting the constrained two-thread topology on a single physical execution core.

Data throughput benchmarks reflect its architectural limits, yielding 14.87 GB/sec large-block read memory bandwidth, 1.98 million Redis SET operations per second, and 3.6 GB/sec static web serving throughput. Because memory and compute are constrained to entry footprint capacities without bundled local storage, the instance functions as a cost-efficient general-purpose tier for lightweight microservices, testing environments, background queue workers, and low-traffic web backends.
description: Amazon Web Services m6in.large is a general-purpose instance featuring an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running on the Nitro hypervisor. The configuration provides 2 vCPUs across 1 physical core, 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory at a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, and a baseline network throughput of 3 Gbps. The instance includes no local storage or GPU acceleration, depending on remote Elastic Block Store volumes for persistent storage. Benchmark data places single-core execution within the middle performance tiers, supported by AVX-512 and cryptographic hardware extensions, whereas multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth reflect entry-level resource boundaries. Given its balanced resources, absence of bundled NVMe, and moderate compute capacity, m6in.large offers practical cost efficiency for microservices, lightweight development environments, API endpoints, and low-concurrency network services.
